usedBy: Use this building block at the bottom of a mobile payment screen. The screen handles sticky positioning and safe-area insets.
overview: A mobile payment-screen footer that groups read-only transaction rows, a total, an optional notice and a full-width action.

default.title: Default
default.text: Use the default surface for a white footer with a subtle top border.

highlight.title: Highlight
highlight.text: Use the highlight surface when the payment screen calls for the elevated light-up background and rounded top corners.

with-notice.title: With notice
with-notice.text: The structured notice sits above the rows. Its title is required; description and icon are optional.

with-notice-highlight.title: Highlight with notice
with-notice-highlight.text: The notice overlaps the body by 16px, keeping the footer surface above the notice.

rich-rows.title: Rich rows
rich-rows.text: Rows can use the existing Transaction List Read Only content, amount, tag and strikethrough props.

many-rows.title: Usage guideline
many-rows.text: Use no more than five items as a screen-level guideline; the component renders every item it receives.

api.intro: The React component accepts Transaction List Read Only rows and leaves business behavior to the consumer.
api.type: Surface appearance. `default` is white with a top border; `highlight` uses the light-up surface and rounded top corners.
api.items: Read-only transaction rows. All supplied rows render; the first uses default density and following rows use compact density.
api.total: Label and value rendered after a divider below the transaction rows.
api.notice: Optional structured notice with a required title, optional description and optional custom icon. When omitted, an Ocean positive check icon is used.
api.action: Consumer-provided action, rendered full width inside the footer body.
api.className: Additional class name for the root element.

platforms.text: The same Footer is available in SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose. iOS keeps `.legacy` as the default style; opt into 2.0 with `.transaction(...)`. Android keeps the legacy overload and adds `OceanTransactionFooter(items, total, button, modifier, type, notice)`. Native notice content is text; sticky positioning and safe-area handling remain the screen's responsibility.

rules: Place the Footer at the bottom of a mobile payment screen; the screen owns sticky positioning and safe-area insets.
Use no more than five items as a screen-level guideline; the component renders every item it receives.
Use TransactionListReadOnly props for row content, including extra information, tags and struck-through values.
Pass a structured notice object with a title; the description and custom icon are optional.
Pass the Ocean button through `action`; do not add a second action inside a row.
